title: ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT. (this line of light stays on.)
format: reel (16.0 s, 1080x1920, 30 fps, 480 frames, H.264 High + AAC 48 kHz stereo, +faststart) with a designed 1080x1920 cover; grid tile = cover y 240-1680
caption:
One bulb is always out. Every ladi, every balcony, every Diwali.

On 101's balcony this line of light stays on: the Fine Tennis Bracelet, one continuous row of small round brilliant clear cubic zirconia, the line about 3 mm wide, each stone in its own gold tone claw cup, closed with a slim box clasp. About 17 cm. ₹1,299.

It stacks with the Baguette Tennis Bracelet from Shop 1, ₹1,599. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

Shubh Deepavali from everyone in the building.

[ fine tennis bracelet · 18k gold tone plated · no spare bulbs needed ]
first_comment: Which bulb is out on your balcony? Every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available #NairaFlore #Diwali #TennisBracelet #DemiFineJewellery #NairaPetite
alt_text: Short video. An illustrated pink Art Deco apartment building on Diwali night; the camera moves in to a first-floor balcony. Its glazed green doors swing open on a dark aubergine room. A string of small glassine bulbs across the top of the doorway and down one side lights up bulb by bulb from left to right; the ninth bulb stays dark. On the balcony ledge a glowing drawn outline turns into a real fine gold-tone tennis bracelet, a continuous row of small clear stones with a slim box clasp, as the bulbs above it light. A sweep of light crosses the stones and the words appear: ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT, 'this line of light stays on.' The dark bulb's filament glows amber once and gives up, and a stone on the bracelet sparkles. A pink paper lantern hangs at the left and a brass plate under the balcony carries the Naira wordmark and FLAT 101. The camera pulls back to the whole building, then a card reads: Flat 101, first floor, Fine Tennis Bracelet, clear cubic zirconia, 18k gold tone plated, ₹1,299, nairaflore.com, Shubh Deepavali in Marathi, and every piece arrives in our blush box, free insured shipping, COD available.

Cover: an illustrated pink Art Deco balcony on Diwali night, its glazed doors open on a dark aubergine room. A string of small warm bulbs runs across the top of the doors and down one side; one bulb is dark. The words ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT, 'this line of light stays on.' On the balcony ledge lies a fine gold-tone tennis bracelet set with one continuous row of small clear stones and a slim box clasp. A pink paper lantern glows at the left; a brass plate below carries the Naira wordmark and FLAT 101.
sound: In-app instrumental, no vocals: a slow evening bansuri piece, raga-like and spacious, no percussion (search 'bansuri ambient', 'diwali instrumental calm'), from 0.6 s, ducked 4 dB under the baked foley. Baked into reel.mp4 (synthesised, tools/sfx.py): 0.0-2.0 s a distant festive murmur over a low street hum (no firecrackers), fading back in over the last 0.6 s for the loop; 0.20 s the series lift-bell (one soft brass ding, ~1.2 s decay); 2.20 s a door latch; 3.40 s a switch click; 5.60 s one glass ting; 8.60 s bulb 9's try, a contact click and a 0.22 s filament fizz (2-5 kHz, so a phone speaker plays it); 12.20 s the end-card chime. Peaks: bell -9.6 dBFS, latch -15.5, switch -16.4, ting -19.8, filament try -16.0 (in reel.mp4; -15.3 in the wav, AAC rounds the click), chime -16.8; ambience RMS -37.

WORLD REVIEW ITEM 4 FIXED INSIDE THE BAY: world/bays/p06.js now builds its own balcony instead of calling the shared NV.build.balcony (the shared builders were not touched). Deck kept in the #F0CABF stone family (empty deck samples hue 12-16 deg, L 71-78; no tan), a 512 px stone grain multiply (p06/assets/stone-grain.png, tools/grain.py), one crisp 2 px #FBF3EC arris, the doorway light a warm-rose (#FF8E86) soft-light at 35 % max, no notches (the front's bottom corners are now the round ends' convex silhouette; the old band() drew them concave), a crisp slab shadow down-right (offset 6/8, blur 2) over a soft one, groove-tone speed lines wrapping the ends. Geometry moved: coping face 32 px (brief 36), front 1062-1204 (brief 1066-1236) so the slab ends 46 px above the plate (review: >= 40). Layer classes kept (nv-arch, p-balshade, p-balshadow, p-spill) so cover mode treats it exactly as before.

DOORS IN TRUE PERSPECTIVE, NOT 1600 px / 72 deg: each leaf is a rotateY about its hinge in a 2600 px perspective centred on the doorway, resting at 88 deg, so it reads 62 px wide at x 150-212 / 868-930 as the brief's cover specifies. At the storyboard's 72 deg in a 1600 px perspective each leaf reads ~150 px wide and covers the O of ONE. Swing 2.2-3.2 s, cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) as briefed. The open glass mirrors the room: dark while the room is dark, warm as it lights.

THE DARK ROOM IS AUBERGINE, NOT NEAR-BLACK: the shared F.darkness multiply is capped in this bay (.75 with the doors shut, .45 open), because at full strength the open doorway sampled (29,18,29), against the brief's own 'never black or near-black grounds'; the dark beat now samples (42,30,49). Shut, the night glass is at half strength so the drawn voile and a faint lamp deep in the room glow through it (the storyboard's 'voile glowing faintly behind'); the reviewer's 'dead slab' note on P7 applied here too.

C-OUTLINE written to render/v3/p06/outlines/fine-tennis-bracelet-00.svg (the brief names work/v3/outlines/, outside this bay's files) by p06/tools/trace.py, REBUILT in fix pass 2 (review fix 1): the cut-out's alpha at 2x render scale, binary closing with disk(6) at render scale, Gaussian sigma 3, contour at .5, each loop resampled at 1 px, decimated to a 0.5 px control polygon and smoothed by Chaikin x3. The clasp hinge's square notch is 14-22 px wide and opens outward, wider than disk(6) can bridge (a disk(6) pass, and then a disk(12) pass, both still left a dip), so inside a 70 x 35 px window round the clasp ONLY it is closed with a 32 px horizontal line, flush with the clasp's foot. Measured: max 1.14 px from the closed alpha edge, max 1.69 px from the raw alpha edge outside the notch window, largest local step 0.10 px at 1x (under 1 px at 2x); 2x crop of the 3.42 s frame viewed. Two loops, the band's outer and inner edge, embedded in the bay. They draw from the clasp round both sides at once (two strokes per loop, 2.6-3.4 s) and retract BEHIND the develop edge (masked), overlapping the photograph by ~180 px. The 3 px #F6EFE6 line keeps its 8 px glow, raised from .45 to .6 because the lighter deck puts the cream line at 1.65-2.19 (median 1.83):1 (review: under 2:1, raise the glow).

THE DEVELOP FOLLOWS THE BULBS: the photograph's soft edge (120 px) sits at the x of the lintel bulb lighting at that moment (piecewise between the bulbs' mid-ramps), not a linear --x over 3.4-4.6 s; it completes at ~4.5 s. The stones under dark bulb 9 develop like the rest (the joke). A faint warm band (screen, 30 % max, masked to the cut-out's alpha) rides the edge. Per-stone ring drawings were tried (stone detection by centreline and by peaks) and dropped: neither placed rings exactly on the stones.

HOPE (review fix 4, raised in fix pass 3): bulb 9's try is an AMBER filament, not a dim ivory bulb: a #FFC98A core at .85 (rx 5.8, ry 6.8, flat to 70 %), a #FFC98A halo at a lit bulb's own 26 px and .75 (screen), a small coil of #FFE2B8 filament between its leads, and the glass filling .25 -> .45 as a lit bulb's does; one sine pulse 8.6-9.5 s (peak 9.05 s), no flicker. Pass 3 applied the director's numbers exactly (halo r 18 -> 26, .35 -> .75; core .65 -> .85). Measured on the final files, a 32 px window on bulb 9 (629, 516), grey mean: 61.8 at rest (8.4, 8.6, 9.5, 9.75 s), 95.6 at 8.8 s, 111.2 at the 9.05 s peak, 96.1 at 9.3 s (reel.mp4; reel-fallback.mp4 61.9 / 111.3 / 61.9), against 97-105 for lit bulbs 8 and 10 (before 82.4 at the peak). Single-frame alternatives measured for the director, not applied: halo .55 -> 103.0, .45 -> 97.8 (just under a lit bulb's window, nearer the storyboard's '.25 -> .7 -> .25'). It reads as a weaker, warmer bulb than its ivory neighbours (the window mean runs past theirs because the amber halo is saturated over its whole 26 px, not because the bulb is brighter), and its halo shows at 391 px wide (_fix3/hope-seq.png). The bracelet's answering sparkle stays at 9.45-10.05 s; the sound's 8.60 s click and fizz still lead the visual peak.

ADDITIONS in the bay: each bulb's own light pooled on the far wall (overlay) and on the frame's plaster (screen, masked to the frame ring), driven with its level; a pooled doorway shadow on the deck while the room is dark, replaced by the rose light as it comes up; the voile gathered 64 px per side so its fold shows beside each folded leaf above and below the words.

SHARED-CODE NOTE (not worked around in shared files): opacity set on the PARENT of a mix-blend-mode layer isolates the blend (Chromium), so the room's overlay lamp painted as plain orange until its opacity reached 1 and then popped (a 2.65 grey-level frame spike at 5.13 s). The original builder's r.light did this; in this bay the opacity now goes on the blended svg itself, and the develop mask goes on the photograph and its multiply shadow separately (a mask on their wrapper would isolate the shadow). Other bays that fade a blended layer through its parent may show the same pop.

SOUND is synthesised (no library samples): murmur, lift-bell, latch, switch, ting, bulb 9's filament try (8.6 s, moved with the visual try) and chime per the brief's times; the instrumental is chosen in-app at posting.

END CARD: the Devanagari 'शुभ दीपावली' (Tiro Devanagari Marathi 44, ink soft, baseline 1104, in the card's 80 ms stagger) is in reel.mp4 and must be signed off by a Marathi reader on the rendered frame before posting; reel-fallback.mp4 carries the brief's fallback 'shubh deepavali.' in Cormorant 40.

DECK AT NIGHT (review fix 2): the whole-deck mauve-grey multiply (#7E5868 .42 -> .16) is gone. In its place a feathered POOL under the doorway only: a trapezoid x 212-868 at the threshold flaring to x 150-930 at the front edge, blur 24, aubergine #6A4A6A multiply at .30 at the threshold falling fast to .14 at 20 % depth and .08 at the front, held a touch denser in the middle (x .7 at the doorway's jambs). DEVIATION from the letter of the fix: an aubergine multiply lowers the stone's chroma at ANY opacity (on this deck, #6A4A6A at only .08 already measures S 31), so the review's own target, L >= 68 AND S >= 35 at tile (220-300, 740-820), cannot be met by the pool alone. The deck also takes the night sky's warm glow, the ledge light's rose #FF8E86 as soft-light at .34 (the deck faces up into the Diwali sky); both fade out as the room's own rose light comes up. Measured in the dark beat: tile (220-300, 740-820) at H 8.9, L 71.3, S 35.7 (reel.mp4 frames 2.4, 3.0 and 3.3 s); the lit deck there H 13, L 75.9, S 42 (before the fix H7 L60 S22, #B08883).

LADI JAMB RUN (review fix 6), a different method from 'start it 10-15 px lower': with the doors open the right leaf's three glazing bars cross x 900 at tile y 297.7-308.0, 421.7-428.3 and 542.0-552.4 (122.2 px apart through the 2600 px perspective at 88 deg). At a uniform 46 px no start clears all three (122.2 mod 46 = 30 puts the bars a third of a cycle apart, while the 20 px glass leaves only a 26 px gap), so a shift alone could never pass. The string is now drawn as TWO runs of the kit's ladi (the documented NV.ladi.create, twice; kit untouched) joined at (900, 200): the lintel's 14 bulbs at 46 px (first bulb 38 px along the wire, so the corner gap to the jamb is ~48 px like the rest, bulb 9 dark) and the jamb's 11 at 40.73 px from y 228.93, a third of a pane, so each bar runs through the bare wire between one bulb's glass and the next one's socket: three bulbs to a pane. The handle still exposes ONE string (h.ladi.bulbs 0-24, global index, colour cycle and breathing wave continuous). Bulb 9 therefore sits at x 629 (was 614). Shut, the bars sit 8 px higher at the hinge and the unlit jamb bulbs still touch them; that state is only on screen while the camera is still moving in (0-2.2 s) and at establishing scale.
